why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line. Check 1 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition requires the second printed line to be "TypeError, because fill must be a single character", and its FAIL condition includes the case where "the second line is NO THROW". Expect line 1 only says padLeft pads on the left with fill, using a space when no fill is given. It says nothing about rejecting a multi-character fill or throwing a TypeError. That stricter test belongs under an Advisory heading, not in the PASS/FAIL conditions. Checks 2, 3 and 4 test only what their lines require: s comes back unchanged when it is already long enough, every exported function has a README section, and npm test exits 0. Naming slugify in Check 3 is fine, because the line covers every export.
